conflicts.quote: At most **one** paid ensure attempt per liquid name per ET day runs **off the trader request path**; the trader HTTP path does not await that Massive I/O.
conflicts.why: Read as a hard one-shot latch after any Massive/compute failure, this turns a transient vendor blip into a permanent `(T, D)` miss when the ring is also empty — colliding with ship-blocking warm-day hit ACs. R1’s presence + in-flight `(T, D)` singleflight already blocks concurrent stampede and per-request tax; it does not by itself forbid a later spaced retry after a failed force-compute while identity is still absent.
conflicts.proposal: Keep desk non-await and no concurrent stampede. Product picks one bound: (a) at most one successful fill per `(T, D)` with spaced off-path retries allowed after hard failure until identity exists or ET date rolls, or (b) a true day-scoped attempt-spent latch after the first Massive attempt (success or fail). R4 must name which; the ensure leaf’s budget mechanism follows.

conflicts.quote: When capture/ensure is **disabled** for the day, research for `(SPY\|QQQ\|IWM, D)` reports honest **`no session book`** and does **not** fabricate an empty book or call Massive on the research read to create one.
conflicts.why: If “capture/ensure disabled” is read to include session-archive store unavailable, this collapses the shipped `session archive not storing` class into `no session book` and breaks the four-way absence distinction UX and the isolation rules require. Store-off already has its own AC-13 outcome.
conflicts.proposal: Narrow AC-10 to ensure skipped / never obtained a paid book / ensure feature off → `no session book`. Keep archive store unavailable exclusively on AC-13 → `session archive not storing` (desk still up).

conflicts.quote: Extra Massive lives **only** on this arm, off the trader request path, ≤1 successful attempt intent per `(T, D)` while identity absent.
conflicts.why: Product + BRIEF lock invoice policy at at-most-one paid fetch per liquid name per ET day while the session identity is still absent — not at-most-one successful compute. Softening to successful-attempt intent silently re-opens same-day retry invoices after a failed force-compute, which AC-8 exists to forbid.
conflicts.proposal: Bound the force-compute arm to at most one Massive fetch per `(T, D)` for the ET day while identity is absent (presence short-circuit + singleflight + no same-day re-arm after a completed attempt, success or fail). Later ET days are new identities.

conflicts.quote: Optional fire-and-forget wake from scanner/ticker warm traffic for those three symbols is allowed only if it never joins the trader HTTP await path.
conflicts.why: Await-only is weaker than the product path rule: extra Massive I/O must not sit on the ticker/scanner request path at all. A request-scoped fire-and-forget that still starts vendor/ensure work can contend with desk latency and rate limits even when HTTP does not await.
conflicts.proposal: Allow at most a non-blocking wake signal into the dedicated ensure worker from warm traffic; Massive and force-compute run only inside that off-path worker, never as request-scoped tasks from ticker/scanner handlers.

conflicts.quote: **Honest degraded outcomes** — disabled ensure, true never-captured, ensure failure, and research miss remain distinguishable and non-fabricating (`absent-is-not-none`).
conflicts.why: Overclaim. UX correctly keeps one shipped miss string for every no-identity cause and bans why-taxonomy (warm cache / not ensured / not a lab name). Disabled ensure, never-captured, and ensure failure are not operator-distinguishable from each other in research copy — only the four shipped classes stay distinct (session miss ≠ ring miss ≠ not storing ≠ unreadable).
conflicts.proposal: Retract cause-level distinguishability among no-identity cases. Keep AC-10–14 as honesty/non-fabrication + four-class separation; do not require miss copy to explain why the identity is absent.

conflicts.quote: **Honest degraded outcomes** — disabled ensure, true never-captured, ensure failure, and research miss remain distinguishable and non-fabricating (`absent-is-not-none`).
conflicts.why: On the research read surface, disabled ensure, ensure failure, never-captured, and ordinary miss all present as the same closed `no session book…` detail (PM’s own AC-10/11/12). Claiming they “remain distinguishable” either invents a fifth/sixth absence class (banned: no ensure-pending / not-a-lab-name rename) or asserts a meaning the wire does not support — UX’s defining failure mode. The four shipped distinctions that must stay are session-miss ≠ ring `no stored snapshot…` ≠ `session archive not storing` ≠ `session book unreadable: <reason>`.
conflicts.proposal: Retract distinguishability among disabled-ensure / never-captured / ensure-failure / research-miss on the research read; keep AC-10–12’s shared honest `no session book` and AC-13/14’s distinct not-storing / unreadable classes.

conflicts.quote: **`review` owns** absence of trader UI (AC-18), not raising the 48 cap (AC-21), closed three-name scope (AC-22), program #3–#7 not absorbed (AC-23), operator-without-trader-UI check (AC-24), and the explicit “authorizes: nothing” research framing (AC-25).
conflicts.why: Trader-chrome absence and the hit-envelope `authorizes: nothing` field can die silently under unrelated dashboard or research-wire refactors while a normal review pass still looks fine. Risk-based verify marks those as `test` (structural affordance / copy byte-identity / wire-field assertion) — matching UX AC-U1/U2/U4. Scope non-goals (48-cap, closed trio, program #3–#7 not absorbed) and positive operator-path-without-trader-UI remain fair `review`.
conflicts.proposal: Reclassify AC-18 and AC-25 as `Verify by: test`; leave AC-21–AC-24 as `review`.

conflicts.quote: Endpoint paths, JSON field names, and operator copy are theirs / R4’s to name; this position only requires an off-path ensure component boundary and the promote-then-force data flow above.
conflicts.why: This ship has no new operator vocabulary to mint. Hit framing, mandatory `source_as_of`, provenance, `authorizes: nothing`, and the four absence `detail` strings are already shipped by `session-chain-archive`. “To name” read as greenfield naming would reopen absence vocabulary and invite banned lab-rename / warm-cache-excuse copy.
conflicts.proposal: R4/UX reuse the shipped session-chain-archive list/load fields and exact §4 strings; they preserve and cite, they do not newly name miss classes or hit framing for this feature.
